career_ladder.note: Judicial officers in Haryana are recruited as Civil Judge (Junior Division) / Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) in the Haryana Civil Service (Judicial Branch) under the Punjab Civil Services (Judicial Branch) Rules, 1951 (as applicable to Haryana) and notification No. GSR 25/Const./Art.234 & 309/2023 dated 07.11.2023. Pay and progression follow the uniform pay matrix of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) as mandated by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India. Officers advance through Assured Career Progression (ACP) scale increments at 5-year intervals and cadre promotions up to the High Court of Punjab and Haryana.

exam_scheme.note: The Haryana Civil Service (Judicial Branch) Examination is conducted jointly by the Haryana Public Service Commission and the High Court of Punjab and Haryana in three stages: Preliminary Examination (Objective screening of 125 MCQs carrying 500 marks), Main Written Examination (5 conventional subjective papers of 3 hours duration each, 900 marks total), and Viva-Voce (200 marks). Final selection merit is prepared on the aggregate of Main written examination and Viva-Voce (out of 1,100 marks).

stages.source_label: HPSC Advt. No. 01/2024 (HCS Judicial Branch) Examination Scheme

papers.paper_name: Preliminary Entrance Examination (Objective Type Law, Current Affairs, Indian Legal & Constitutional History)
papers.negative_marking: 0.8 mark (20% or one-fifth) deducted for each incorrect answer out of 4 marks per question (125 questions total). Mandatory 5th bubble rule: unattempted questions require darkening bubble 'E'; failure to darken any circle incurs 0.8 mark penalty; leaving more than 10% questions (13 questions) un-darkened causes immediate disqualification.
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum qualifying score of 150 marks for General / UR candidates (100 marks for all reserved categories of Haryana except EWS). Candidates equal to 10 times the number of advertised vacancies (plus bracketed candidates) qualify for the Main written examination. Marks do not count towards the final merit list.

stages.source_label: HPSC Advt. No. 01/2024 (HCS Judicial Branch) Examination Scheme

papers.paper_name: Paper I: Civil Law - I (CPC, Punjab Courts Act, Contract Act, Partnership Act, Sale of Goods Act, Specific Relief Act, Evidence Act, Haryana Urban Rent Control Act)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 33% marks required in each individual written paper

papers.paper_name: Paper II: Civil Law - II (Hindu Law, Mohammadan Law, Customary Law, Law of Registration and Limitation)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 33% marks required in each individual written paper

papers.paper_name: Paper III: Criminal Law (Indian Penal Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, Indian Evidence Act)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 33% marks required in each individual written paper

papers.paper_name: Paper IV: English (English Essay 100 marks, Precis 25 marks, Words & Phrases 25 marks, Comprehension 25 marks, Corrections 25 marks)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 33% marks required in each individual written paper

papers.paper_name: Paper V: Language - Hindi in Devnagri Script (Translation 20 marks, Explanation prose & poetry 30 marks, Composition essay/idioms/corrections 50 marks)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 33% marks required in each individual written paper; minimum 50% qualifying marks in aggregate of all written papers (45% for SC, BC, PwBD, ESM) to qualify for Viva-Voce

stages.source_label: HPSC Advt. No. 01/2024 (HCS Judicial Branch) Examination Scheme

papers.qualifying_threshold: Tests personal qualities, alertness, intelligence, and general outlook. Candidates equal to 3 times the advertised vacancies (plus bracketed candidates) are called for interview based on Main written marks. Appearance in viva-voce is mandatory. Candidates must secure at least 50% marks (45% for SC, BC, PwBD, ESM) in aggregate of Main written examination and Viva-Voce to be eligible for appointment.

financial_package.note: Judicial officers in Haryana receive remuneration governed by the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) uniform pay matrix as mandated by the Supreme Court of India in All India Judges Association v. Union of India. Recruits are placed in revised SNJPC Pay Scale Level J-1 (₹77,840–₹1,36,520; unrevised scale ₹27,700–₹44,770).
financial_package.pay_source_label: HPSC Advt. No. 01/2024 & Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) in WP(C) 643/2015
financial_package.estimate_note: Gross salary computed from SNJPC Level J-1 entry basic ₹77,840 + 58% DA (₹45,147) + judicial House Rent Allowance (HRA 8% to 24% or designated official judicial bungalow) + judicial sumptuary, robe, medical, conveyance, and domestic help allowances. In-hand estimate accounts for statutory deductions including 10% NPS contribution (Basic + DA = ₹12,299), Group Insurance Scheme (GIS), and Haryana Professional Tax.
official_perks: Designated independent judicial bungalow / official residence in the Judicial Officers' Colony of the posting district
Official staff car / conveyance facility with driver entitlement and monthly fuel allowance
Monthly sumptuary allowance and annual robe / dress maintenance allowance per SNJPC recommendations
Comprehensive cashless medical treatment and reimbursement for officer and dependent family members
Residential orderly / attendant allowance and reimbursement of domestic help charges
Reimbursement of electricity and water charges up to prescribed monthly units, plus official mobile and broadband facilities
Substantial judicial pension and gratuity entitlements under statutory judicial service rules
